P E G tube care. Site care, feeding and medicines, step by step.
Step one. Know the PEG tube: a percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy, used for longer term enteral feeding. Know its indications, its contraindications, and how it is inserted and managed.
Step two. Assemble your equipment. Confirm the physician's order. You need a dressing set, sterile normal saline, non-sterile and sterile gloves, a sterile gauze dressing, and face masks.

Step three. Prepare the patient. A newly inserted PEG is one within its first week. Explain the procedure, raise the head slightly, draw the curtains, ask visitors to leave, and confirm the patient's identity.

Step four. Change the dressing at least daily. Wash your hands, put on non-sterile gloves and a mask, and take precautions against aspiration. Remove the old dressing carefully, and check for infection and skin integrity.

Step five. Critical point. Use strict aseptic technique. With sterile gloves, slide the outer bumper about one centimetre away from the skin. Gently press around the tube to check for drainage, and inspect the tube for wear. Clean the stoma with zero point nine percent sodium chloride, in a circular, outward motion, then rinse thoroughly.
Step six. Rotate the outer bumper ninety degrees, and slide it back over the exit site.

Step seven. Dressing rules. Put sterile gauze over the site only if it is leaking, or the tube could be dislodged. Never put gauze under the outer bumper, and never cover the tube. Write the date and time on the tape, and label every tube. Once the site has healed, after about one week, no dressing is needed.

Step eight. Critical point. Feeding can begin only twenty four hours after insertion, with peristalsis present, and a doctor's order. Sit the patient in semi-Fowler's position, and verify the feed type and volume.
Step nine. Assess the residual gastric contents as per policy. To check patency, let thirty millilitres of water flow into the tube by gravity. Never force it.
Step ten. Follow the correct procedure for continuous or intermittent feeds. Flush the tube when policy requires, clean the syringe after use, and replace the bag and tubing at the set interval.
Step eleven. Watch for intolerance: nausea, vomiting, or abdominal distension. Stop the feed, sit the patient up, assess, and inform the doctor.
Step twelve. Give medicines via the PEG as per policy: one at a time, flushing before, between, and after each one.
Step thirteen. Show empathy and reassurance, respect dignity and privacy, and escalate leakage, infection, or displacement promptly.
Step fourteen. Document the patient's tolerance of feeds and medicines, and the condition of the stoma site. Report any displacement, blockage, or complication to the physician.
Watch, take the quiz, then get signed off.
